newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - May 29.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - May 29.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for REUTERS by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi Tel:3324842, 3351006, 3761233 Fax:+91-11-3351006 Internet: biznis@giasbm01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
The Hindustan Times
CONGRESS CHIEF DISPLAYS HUGE SUPPORT, FILES PAPERS

Sitaram Kesri entered the race for the post of Congress party president, showing that he commanded enough support in the party to win. A contest is inevitable because his two rivals -- Sharad Pawar and Rajesh Pilot -- are in the fray. As many as 67 sets of nomination papers were filed in Kesri's favour, as against three each for Pawar and Pilot, to show that he commanded an overwhelming majority support in the All India Congress Committee and the states and his election was a foregone conclusion. Kesri surpassed Narasimha Rao's record of 57 nominations in his favour in 1992.
The Economic Times
MINISTRY DRAWS UP MODEL FUEL SUPPLY PACT

The Power Ministry has finalised a model fuel supply agreement (FSA) to enable power companies to obtain fuel supplies through legally enforceable commercial agreements. The model FSA provisions include the sharing of fuel risk by the equity holders of a power company, mandatory tripartite agreement between fuel supplier, transporter and power firm, third party fuel sale by fuel suppliers in case state electricity boards fail to consume the allocated amount, payment of damages by fuel suppliers if they fail to supply the committed amount and provision by federal government holding companies of guarantees for subsidiaries and divisions.
SAIL NET PLUNGES 60 PER CENT

The Steel Authority of India's profit after tax plunged 60 percent to 5.27 billion rupees in 96/97 (April-March). It was 13.18 billion rupees in 1995/96. This is well below the 6.53 billion rupees profit after tax estimated in the performance budget. Sales and other income also dropped 2.56 percent or 3.87 billion rupees in 1996/97. The performance budget had indicated a marginal increase in income. Expenditure too has declined by 1.46 billion rupees. Interest payments increased by 4.83 billion rupees or almost 60 percent. This leads to a sharply lower gross profit (before depreciation and tax) of 12.92 billion rupees as against 19 billion rupees in 1995/ 96.
100 PCT FOREIGN PROPOSALS BEING RE-EVALUATED

The Industry Ministry is re-evaluating proposals from multinationals wishing to set up wholly-owned subsidiaries in India. It will now pay more attention to issues such as the level of technology, the areas of proposed investment and the multinational's existing businesses in India. Senior officials said it is wrong to assume that the Foreign Investment Promotion Board (FIPB) will automatically clear all kinds of foreign investment proposals. As per FIPB norms now, full foreign ownership will be allowed in case the investment is a holding operation. All subsequent/downstream investments will require prior government approval.
COLGATE-PALMOLIVE GROSS PROFIT SLIPS

Colgate-Palmolive (India) recorded a net profit of 780.3 million rupees for the year up to March 31, compared to 775.8 rupees netted in 1995/96. Sales grew by 13 percent at 9.62 billion rupees against the previous year's 8.5 billion rupees. Gross profit slipped to 1552.6 million rupees from 1564.2 million rupees a year ago. But Colgate managed to contain its interest burden at 2.4 million rupees against 5.5 million in 1995/96. Company officials say the flat growth was due to the excise duty cuts in the last two Union budgets.
IMPORTS OF EDIBLE OILS TO BE UP

India's demand for imported edible oils is slated to rise. Imports of RBD palmolein, sunflower and soya oils are expected to be around 175,000 to 200,000 tonnes during June 1997. Sources point out that contracting for around 20,000 tonnes of palmolein for July shipment has been done. Edible oil importers have started booking heavily in the international market, mainly due to the low prices quoted by Malaysian shippers for the future deliveries. After touching a high of $600 FOB per tonne and above during March-April 1997, prices are now ruling at $590 per tonne. The June shipment is quoted at $572, July at $569 and August at $560.
Financial Express
CENTRE TO PROMOTE BOT PROJECTS

The government will provide loans to help entrepreneurs in the road and port sectors to take up build-operate-transfer (BOT) projects as investment inflow in this segment has been sluggish. The minister of surface transport said the private investor is always uncertain about the volume of traffic switching to BOT facility. He said the government is aware of the problems and risks involved in the BOT projects, which have to be identified and managed. The minister said the government is actively considering the grant of property development rights to private road developers to supplement the revenue and improve viability of the projects.
EXPORTERS CAN TRANSFER FUNDS TO OVERSEAS ACCOUNT

Indian corporate exporters incorporated as public/private limited companies will be permitted to remit trade-related advances from the exchange earner's foreign currency account to their overseas importer clients without the Reserve Bank's prior approval. Such advances can be made up to a ceiling of $3 million at any point. The facility is part of the RBI's slack season credit policy for the first half of 1997/98 (April-March) fiscal. The Bank's instructions to authorised dealers say that if the advances exceed the ceiling amount, a guarantee from a reputed international bank outside India or a standby letter has to be obtained.
NATIONAL BOURSE TO IMPLEMENT ROLLING SETTLEMENT

In three months, the national bourse (NSE) is expected to introduce a rolling settlement in the dematerialised segment. It is proposed to hold settlements every day and to settle trades on a T+5 cycle, that is a trade would be settled five days after it is carried out. The NSE deputy managing director said the move forms part of measures proposed to be taken by NSE to boost investor participation in the depository. He had said the NSE is also considering reduction in transaction charges in the demateriailsed segment and mooted a proposal whereby small investors in the dematerialised mode could deposit these shares with the depository participant.
Business Standard
RESERVE BANK GIVES PERSONAL BANKING A PUSH

The Reserve Bank of India has softened its stance on branch licensing and allowed banks to open personal banking branches. The move will create competition for non-banking finance companies. Union Bank of India and the Corporation Bank have been allowed to open branches specifically for personal banking to deliver both liability and asset products. The Reserve Bank has granted six licences to Corporation Bank to open personal banking branches. The State Bank of India (SBI) also, plans to go into personal banking in a big way. The proposal at SBI is to use the existing branch network to deliver personal banking products.
GARMENT MAKERS DRAW UP PLAN TO BOOST EXPORTS

The apparel export promotion council (AEPC) has submitted an action plan to the government to boost export of garments. The garments sector is a major foreign exchange earner, accounting for 15 percent of the nearly $35 billion annual exports. The AEPC chairman said the council wants the government to adopt a positive policy regarding garment exports in order to hit this year's export target at $5.25 billion especially in the wake of a noticeable decline in conventional exports due to sagging demand in Europe and formation of regional trading blocs. He said recession led to a shortfall of 14.7 percent in garment exports in value terms in April and May this year.
INDUSTRY GROWTH MAY DROP TO 6 PCT

Industrial growth of six percent in 1997/98 has become a distinct possibility following indications that the industrial growth in 1996/97 is unlikely to exceed 7.20 percent. Advance estimates collated by the Industry Ministry for 24 industries provide a major pointer to a less than 7.2 percent growth in 1996/97. The industry ministry is keeping these figures under wraps, although the ministry has been very regular in putting out these figures at the beginning of the year. The index for the 24 industries comprises primarily the core and infrastructure sector and carries a weightage of 50 percent in the full CSO index.
The Observer
IIFT FOR SETTING UP MARITIME GUILD

The Indian Institute of Foreign Trade (IIFT) has suggested to the Commerce Ministry to set up a maritime guild. The guild should have vessel owners, main line agents, sub-agents, feeder line operators, freight forwarders, slot charterers and customs house agents. A study report by IIFT recommended that instead of two separate authorities being involved as at present, the relief due on exports should be granted by a single authority based on documents of proof of exports. It has been shown that while manufacturer exporters have to submit AR-4 form for satisfying six different authorities for the claim/cancellation of bond, it can be reduced to three without any problem.
DESTINATION INDIA SEMINARS TO WOO US INVESTORS

A series of 'Destination India' seminars will be held in the United States to attract more American investment in India, especially to small and medium industries. The seminars will be a jointly organised by the government of India and the Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce and Industry with local participation. The first seminar will be organised in Boston in September. The focus will be on information technology including hardware, software, electronic components and telecom, medical instrumentation, precision machinery, environmental technology and biotechnology. Other seminars will be held in Chicago, Washington DC and a city in the south.
NON-BANKING FIRMS MAY BE BROUGHT UNDER CONTROL

The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) is contemplating bringing all non-banking finance companies (NBFCs) under Deposit Insurance and Credit Guarantee Corporation (DICGC). This is to protect the interests of depositors. According to sources in the RBI, the DICGC, which works under the RBI will be asked to frame schemes for the NBFCs particularly in the area of deposit insurance. The proposal to introduce insurance scheme for the NBFCs was submitted about a couple of months back. After the CRB Capitals fiasco, the RBI top-rung had a relook into the proposal and reportedly decided to press the DICGC into action.
